options.text: North–south direction; the marked end is the North pole of the magnet.
East–west direction; the marked end is the South pole of the magnet.
North–south direction while the magnet is still swinging.
A direction that any ordinary iron bar would show the same way when hung.

stem:
The diagram shows a bar magnet hanging from a thread so it can turn freely, away from other magnets. After it settles, Sonia marks the end that points toward geographic north.

What has she found?

teacher.key_rationale: A freely suspended magnet settles along north–south. The end pointing toward geographic north is the North pole. Read it after it settles; an ordinary iron bar does not reliably show the same resting direction.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source cylinders into a freely suspended bar magnet settled along geographic north–south.
